summary: Round 4. All four round-3 blocking findings are dealt with, and I probed each one. The width-wise strap loop (strap_under/l/r) overlaps nothing: it is 4.2 mm from the VTX and 14.2 mm above the stack, it closes at about 175 mm of the 250 mm strap, and the VTX sits clear at x -27.5..0.5. The connector extrapolation is gone: the XT60 is back at its plain 60 A rating. The 95 mm Lollipop reaches its head with about 18 mm spare (path about 77 mm). The receiver antenna V is at the roof front behind the lens. Every BOM row has a buy link. The cradle walls now start on the tab. It still fails on one major point. Betaflight motor_output_limit = 74 is a real, legitimate configured cap, but the `power` pass depends on it and the generated ASSEMBLY.md and WIRING.md never tell Spencer to set it (WIRING.md even lists 35 A motor peaks). It also has to be documented as a central estimate: by my calculation the real peak is about 60-61 A against 60 A, still physically safe because that rating is for 1 minute.

findings.issue: The `power` pass depends on a Betaflight setting that the build package never tells Spencer to make. On the mechanism itself: Betaflight `motor_output_limit` is real. It is applied in the mixer to every motor's final output. On the BLHeli_S 55 A ESC there is no firmware current limit at all, so this output cap is the only cap available, and it is the same kind of cap tvc_drone uses (MOT_SPIN_MAX). I accept it as an honest configured cap under ENGINEERING.md 10b, with one condition: it has to actually be configured. Today `set motor_output_limit = 74` appears only in DESIGN.md (assembly step 9). The generated deliverables leave it out. ASSEMBLY.md has 13 steps and none mentions it. WIRING.md shows each motor at a 35.08 A peak in its Loads table, but 14.22 A on the phase wires and 57.44 A on the XT60, with no word about where the cap comes from. A builder who follows ASSEMBLY.md and WIRING.md flies at 100 % output, about 140 A through a connector the report says sees 57.4 A. The requirement then describes a different quad from the one that was built.
findings.fix: Engine (general, so tvc_drone gets it too): in wiring_out / ship, print every `electrical.limits` entry with its `why` as a 'Configure before the first flight' section in WIRING.md, plus a numbered final step in ASSEMBLY.md's electrical list (here: Betaflight CLI `set motor_output_limit = 74`, `save`, then check the Blackbox/OSD current peak on the first punch-out). In the WIRING.md Loads table, show the capped peak next to the catalog peak, with the limit as its source. Add a test that a project with `electrical.limits` gets the configure step in both files.

findings.issue: The cap's current estimate is slightly optimistic, and the comment calls it conservative. project.yaml and DESIGN.md say 35.08 x 0.74^3 = 14.22 A is 'on the high side' because motor efficiency rises at part load. The direction is wrong. At 74 % duty the I*R drop shrinks faster than the drive voltage, so loaded rpm falls by less than 26 %. With roughly 60 mOhm of motor + ESC resistance, rpm comes out near 0.756 of full rather than 0.74. Battery current = duty x motor current = 0.74 x 0.756^2 x 35.08, about 14.8 A per motor, so roughly 60-61 A total against the 60 A rating. A full pack (25.2 V against the 24.0 V test voltage) adds a few percent more. In physical terms this is fine: the XT60's 60 A rating is for 1 minute and the bursts are 5 s. But the 4 % margin on paper (0.957) is inside the model's error, and the T/W >= 6 requirement leaves no room to cut the limit to 72 %. The same correction makes the thrust estimate conservative (0.57 rather than 0.548 of full thrust), so `twr` is fine.
findings.fix: Correct the wording: the propeller-law current is a central estimate, not an upper bound. Make the first-flight Blackbox/OSD current check the gate (peak <= 60 A on a full pack, else lower the limit by 1-2 %). Optionally catalogue the iFlight throttle table (it lists current at 50/60/75 % throttle) and use the measured 75 % row instead of the scaling law.

findings.issue: The XT60 pigtail has very little room to turn. The 12 AWG leads (3.6 mm OD, catalog wire.silicone) leave the cradle's front stops at x -44.55 on the centreline (pins stacked in z). They must be at |y| >= 14.3 (pillar half-width 12.5 + wire radius) by the rear pillar face at x -37.5. That is 14.3 mm sideways in 7 mm forward, about a 5 mm centreline bend radius (1.4 x OD), right at the solder cup. The BOM's '20 mm' heat-shrink over that joint would run past x -37.5 into the pillar. The route check passes because its tube model has no bend radius and no stiff joint section. It can be built with flexible silicone wire, but the bend sits right at the solder cups, and every battery plug-in loads those cups.
findings.fix: Either add a build note (solder the leads pre-bent at 90 deg towards -y, use 8-10 mm heat-shrink on the 12 AWG joints, and change the BOM line), or give the turn about 8 more mm: move the XT60 to x -67 with the tab to -80, or narrow the rear pillar's y extent on the lead side.

findings.issue: The single battery strap sits 14.5 mm ahead of the pack's centre (band x 4.5..24.5 on a pack spanning x -41..41), because the VTX takes up x -27.5..0.5 underneath. The rear 55 mm of the pack is held only by the pad's friction and can lift or yaw about the strap in hard manoeuvres and crashes. I probed the strap loop itself and it is now correct (see summary).
findings.fix: Acceptable as is, with the anti-slip pad. If the pack shifts in testing, add a second strap band at x about -36 (the gap between the rear pillar and the tab), or move the VTX 6-8 mm further back so the band can sit closer to x 0.

findings.issue: The antenna head (x -83.5..-72.5, y -16..-5, z 48-68) and its tube bending up past the tab end (z about 43-48 at y -10.5) sit right where the fingers grip the battery's XT60 plug to plug it in and pull it out (plug at x -70..-79, |y| <= 4, z 29-45). The connector_access probe only sweeps the 8.1 x 16 mm connector section, not a hand. Each battery swap will catch the antenna. It is clear of the prop discs: 16.5 mm above prop_3.
findings.fix: Mirror the antenna to the +y side, or move its exit forward of the plug zone (up through a slot at about x -45, y -12), so that y -12..+12 behind the tab is free for fingers.

findings.issue: Stale and missing numbers in the documents. DESIGN.md line 30 still reads '-> 12.6 (requirement >= 6)'. Line 115 says '73 %' where everything else says 74 %. The risks list says 'Flight time 13 min' where the report says 11.96. WIRING.md's headline 'hover time 11.96 min' still has no 'ideal hover-only estimate; freestyle about 3-5 min' caveat (round-3 fix; it reached only the requirement's `why`). XT60 mass is 0.0 g in the report (no weight_g in the catalog). The battery's own lead length (140 mm, `supplied`) is assumed, not catalogued. The motor phase lead gauge and length are still not catalogued (carried from round 3).
findings.fix: Fix the three DESIGN.md lines. Make wiring_out print the estimate caveat. Add XT60 weight_g (Amass, about 4 g per pair) and the CNHL lead length/gauge and the XING2 lead gauge/length to the catalog, each with a source.

findings.issue: Carried from round 3, still to check on the bench: at 0 deg tilt the cheek tips may show at the image sides, and at 35-40 deg the roof tongue's front corners may show in the top corners. Both are out of view at the 25 deg home tilt.
findings.fix: Check with the camera fitted. Chamfer the cheek tips or round the roof corners if they show.

findings.issue: Carried: the first arm bending mode is about 165 Hz, in the gyro noise band, and PETG-CF sits directly on a motor base that can reach 70-80 C. Both are acknowledged in the DESIGN.md risks.
findings.fix: Keep the hover + Blackbox gyro check in the build notes. Consider a 0.5-1 mm standoff ring under the motor base.
